newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended higher as the strong Swiss swap market and a favourable tone in U.S. and German bonds propelled Swiss prices higher.
One cash trader said that the spread between cash bond yields and swaps has narrowed by roughly 10 basis points in the past week.
"Bonds haven't performed as well as swaps," the trader said. Swaps were helped by a drop in Swiss money market rates as recent month-end tightness began to abate.
"In terms of swaps it has been a good day," a swaps trader said. But he said there was little business in the market.
Swap rates "are significantly lower. I think the end-of- month fall-off in tightness in the cash market helped that," the swaps dealer said.
Gains in the three-month Euroswiss contract traded on LIFFE, which the trader saw a correction in a technically oversold market, also helped the short end.
Five-year swap rates for example, quoted late Friday at 3.42/3.48, were about eight basis points lower than Thursday's open.
But dealers said the swap market was illiquid, and this also may have contributed to the drop in swap rates.
"People are marking the market away from doing business. They are marking the prices away from where people be interested," the swaps trader said.
The Confederate bond futures contract extended Thursday's gains. Response to the Swiss federal government's latest bond auction completed Thursday helped to buoy the market.
The contract closed at its high for the day of 115.45 which compared with the contract high of 115.80 set October 9.
